00002| title: generateStaticParams
00003| description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
00007| 
00008| `generateStaticParams` can be used with:
00009| 
00010| - [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
00011| - [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
00012| - [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
00013| 
00014| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00017|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00018| 
00019|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00020|     slug: post.slug,
00021|   }))
00022| }
00023| 
00024| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00025| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00026| export default async function Page({
00027|   params,
00028| }: {
00029|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00030| }) {
00031|   const { slug } = await params
00032|   // ...
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00038| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00039|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00040| 
00041|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00042|     slug: post.slug,
00043|   }))
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00047| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00048| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00049|   const { slug } = await params
00050|   // ...
00051| }
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**:
00055| >
00056| > - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00057| > - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
00058| > - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
00059| > - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
00060| > - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
00061| > - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
00062| 
00063| ## Parameters
00064| 
00065| `options.params` (optional)
00066| 
00067| If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
00068| 
00069| The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).

00073| `generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
00074| 
00075| - Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
00076| - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.

00271|     slug: post.slug,
00272|   }))
00273| }
00274| ```
00275| 
00276| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00277| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00278| export const dynamicParams = false
00279| 
00280| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00281|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00282|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00283| 
00284|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00285|     slug: post.slug,
00286|   }))
00287| }
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| #### All paths at runtime
00291| 
00292| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00293| 
00294| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
00295| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00296|   return []
00297| }
00298| ```
00299| 
00300| > **Good to know:**
00301| >
00302| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00303| 
00304| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
00305| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00306| ```
00307| 
00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00311| 
00312| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00313| 
00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00321| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00336| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00337|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00338| }
00339| 
00340| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00341|   const { id } = await params
00342|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00343|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00350| 
00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00352| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00353|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00354| }
00355| 
00356| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id
00359|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00366| ) {
00367|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00368|   return Response.json(post)
00369| }
00370| ```
00371| 
00372| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00373| 
00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00377| 
00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00384| 
00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00388| 
00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00390| 
00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00392| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00393| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00394|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00395| 
00396|   return products.map((product) => ({
00397|     category: product.category.slug,
00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }
00401| 
00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```
00410| 
00411| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00412| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00413| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00414|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00415| 
00416|   return products.map((product) => ({
00417|     category: product.category.slug,
00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }) {
00423|   // ...
00424| }
00425| ```
00426| 
00427| #### Generate params from the top down
00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00432| // Generate segments for [category]
00433| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00434|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00435| 
00436|   return products.map((product) => ({
00437|     category: product.category.slug,
00438|   }))
00439| }
00440| 
00441| export default function Layout({
00442|   params,
00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00454| 
00455|   return products.map((product) => ({
00456|     category: product.category.slug,
00457|   }))
00458| }
00459| 
00460| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00461|   // ...
00462| }
00463| ```
00464| 
00465| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00466| 
00467| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00468| 
00469| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00470| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00471| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00472| export async function generateStaticParams({
00473|   params: { category },
00474| }: {
00475|   params: { category: string }
00476| }) {
00477|   const products = await fetch(
00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```
00494| 
00495| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00496| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00498| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00499|   const products = await fetch(
00500|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00501|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00502| 
00503|   return products.map((product) => ({
00504|     product: product.id,
00505|   }))
00506| }
00507| 
00508| export default function Page({ params }) {
00509|   // ...
00510| }
00511| ```
00512| 
00513| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00514| 
00515| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00516| 
00517| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00518| 
00519| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00520| export async function generateStaticParams({
00521|   params: { category },
00522| }: {
00523|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00524| }) {
00525|   const products = await fetch(
00526|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00527|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00528| 
00529|   return products.map((product) => ({
00530|     product: product.id,
00531|   }))
00532| }
00533| ```
00534| 
00535| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00536| 
00537| ## Version History
00538| 
00539| | Version   | Changes                            |
00540| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00541| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

00289| 
00290| #### All paths at runtime
00291| 
00292| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00293| 
00294| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"

00297| }

00299| 
00300| > **Good to know:**
00301| >
00302| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00303| 
00304| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"

00306| ```
00307| 
00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00311| 
00312| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00313| 
00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher

00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```

00344| }
00345| ```

00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:

00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"

00354| }

00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id

00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>

00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).

00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.

00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up

00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.

00395|

00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }

00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```

00415|

00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }

00424| }

00428|

00438|   }))
00439| }

00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())

00474| }: {

00476| }) {

00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```

00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function

00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00321| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00336| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00337|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00338| }
00339| 
00340| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00341|   const { id } = await params
00342|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00343|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00350| 
00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00352| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00353|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00354| }
00355| 
00356| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id
00359|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00366| ) {
00367|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00368|   return Response.json(post)
00369| }
00370| ```
00371| 
00372| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00373| 
00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00377| 
00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00384| 
00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00388| 
00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00390| 
00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00392| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00393| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00394|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00395| 
00396|   return products.map((product) => ({
00397|     category: product.category.slug,
00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }
00401| 
00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```
00410| 
00411| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00412| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00413| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00414|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00415| 
00416|   return products.map((product) => ({
00417|     category: product.category.slug,
00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }) {
00423|   // ...
00424| }
00425| ```
00426| 
00427| #### Generate params from the top down
00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00432| // Generate segments for [category]
00433| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00434|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00435| 
00436|   return products.map((product) => ({
00437|     category: product.category.slug,
00438|   }))
00439| }
00440| 
00441| export default function Layout({
00442|   params,
00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00454| 
00455|   return products.map((product) => ({
00456|     category: product.category.slug,
00457|   }))
00458| }
00459| 
00460| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00461|   // ...
00462| }
00463| ```
00464| 
00465| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00466| 
00467| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00468| 
00469| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00470| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00471| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00472| export async function generateStaticParams({
00473|   params: { category },
00474| }: {
00475|   params: { category: string }
00476| }) {
00477|   const products = await fetch(
00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```
00494| 
00495| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00496| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00498| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00499|   const products = await fetch(
00500|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00501|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00502| 
00503|   return products.map((product) => ({
00504|     product: product.id,
00505|   }))
00506| }
00507| 
00508| export default function Page({ params }) {
00509|   // ...
00510| }
00511| ```
00512| 
00513| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00514| 
00515| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00516| 
00517| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00518| 
00519| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00520| export async function generateStaticParams({
00521|   params: { category },
00522| }: {
00523|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00524| }) {
00525|   const products = await fetch(
00526|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00527|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00528| 
00529|   return products.map((product) => ({
00530|     product: product.id,
00531|   }))
00532| }
00533| ```
00534| 
00535| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00536| 
00537| ## Version History
00538| 
00539| | Version   | Changes                            |
00540| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00541| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |
00542|

[`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) automatically optimizes your fonts (including custom fonts) and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.

It includes **built-in automatic self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no [layout shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls).

You can also conveniently use all [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/). CSS and font files are downloaded at build time and self-hosted with the rest of your static assets. **No requests are sent to Google by the browser.**

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

[`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) automatically optimizes your fonts (including custom fonts) and removes external network requests for improved privacy and performance.

It includes **built-in automatic self-hosting** for any font file. This means you can optimally load web fonts with no [layout shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls).

You can also conveniently use all [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/). CSS and font files are downloaded at build time and self-hosted with the rest of your static assets. **No requests are sent to Google by the browser.**

events.content:
Migrated the entire project to the Next.js App Router and removed the `pages` directory.

Summary of changes:
- Created `app/layout.tsx` replacing `_app.js` + `_document.js`, using `next/font` for Inter, global metadata, and the shared header/footer nav.
- Created `app/page.tsx` from `pages/index.js`, replacing `getServerSideProps` with async data fetch + `revalidate`.
- Created `app/blog/page.tsx` from `pages/blog/index.js`, replacing `getStaticProps` with ISR fetch.
- Created `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` from `pages/blog/[id].js`, replacing `getStaticPaths` with `generateStaticParams`, `getStaticProps` with async fetch + `revalidate`, and `Head` with `generateMetadata`.
- Created `app/not-found.tsx` replacing `pages/404.js` and `app/global-error.tsx` replacing `pages/_error.js`.
- Migrated API routes to Route Handlers:
  - `app/api/posts/route.ts` (GET/POST)
  - `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` (GET/PUT/DELETE)
- Updated `components/AppProvider.tsx` with types and `'use client'` for the context provider.
- Deleted `pages/`, `pages/_app.js`, `_document.js`, `_error.js`, `404.js`, all route pages, and API routes.

Verification: `npx next build` completed successfully, generating static pages for `/`, `/blog`, and the 10 prerendered blog post routes.
